title: FactAppeal: Identifying Epistemic Factual Appeals in News Media
authors: Guy Mor-Lan; Tamir Sheafer; Shaul R. Shenhav
task_description: Identify whether and how factual statements are anchored by external sources/evidence.
inputs: 3,226 English news sentences with claim/source spans.
outputs_or_labels: Span labels for factual statements and source mentions; source type, namedness, role/credentials, direct/indirect quotation and related epistemic features.
pipeline_gap_filled: Claim ownership; source attribution; reported speech; claim-to-source edges.
artifact_access_status: paper page/PDF verified; separate dataset download not verified
evidence_basis: ACL abstract states a manually annotated dataset of 3,226 sentences with span-level claims/sources and fine-grained attribution features, including direct/indirect quotation.
limitations: News-domain only; does not require recursive multi-hop evidence chains or disagreement labels.
why_relevant: Closest match for explicit ownership and epistemic attribution annotations; strong seed for an attribution-aware claim graph.

title: Who Said What: Formalization and Benchmarks for the Task of Quote Attribution
authors: Wenjie Zhong; Jason Naradowsky; Hiroya Takamura; Ichiro Kobayashi; Yusuke Miyao
task_description: Benchmark quote attribution by pairing textual utterances with speakers across English and Chinese datasets.
inputs: Quoted utterances, surrounding literary/news context, candidate speakers.
outputs_or_labels: Speaker identity for each quote; benchmark scores and error analysis.
pipeline_gap_filled: Reported speech attribution; source/claim ownership boundary.
artifact_access_status: paper page/PDF verified; constituent datasets not independently verified
evidence_basis: ACL abstract explicitly defines quote attribution and says the paper benchmarks all available English/Chinese datasets.
limitations: Speaker attribution is not epistemic evidence attribution; no support/attack or recursive chains.
why_relevant: Useful control for attribution extraction before evidence reasoning.

title: A Two-stage Sieve Approach for Quote Attribution
authors: Grace Muzny; Michael Fang; Angel Chang; Dan Jurafsky
task_description: Link quotations to speaker mentions and speaker entities in literary text.
inputs: Literary quotations, speaker mentions, speaker entities.
outputs_or_labels: Over 6,000 annotations linking quotes to mentions and entities; quote-to-speaker labels.
pipeline_gap_filled: Reported speech; recursive attribution entity resolution.
artifact_access_status: paper page/PDF verified; dataset URL not independently verified
evidence_basis: ACL abstract states QuoteLi3 contains more than 6,000 annotations and separates quote→mention from mention→entity.
limitations: Literary dialogue is not source-backed factual claims; no evidence sufficiency or contradiction.
why_relevant: Provides a decomposable attribution subtask and intermediate artifacts.

title: HoVer: A Dataset for Many-Hop Fact Extraction And Claim Verification
authors: Yichen Jiang; Shikha Bordia; Zheng Zhong; Charles Dognin; Maneesh Singh; Mohit Bansal
task_description: Retrieve distributed evidence across multiple Wikipedia articles and verify claims requiring many hops.
outputs_or_labels: Veracity labels plus multi-sentence gold evidence sets for 2–6 hop chains.
pipeline_gap_filled: Recursive evidence chains; claim-to-source traversal; evidence set completeness.
artifact_access_status: paper page/PDF verified; dataset download not independently verified
license_status: CC BY-SA 4.0 reported in a later scholarly artifact; not re-verified from original release
evidence_basis: ACL page identifies HoVer as a many-hop evidence extraction and claim verification dataset; later ACL evidence describes 2–6 hop chains and complementary evidence.
limitations: Wikipedia-only; attribution/ownership and disagreement are not central.
why_relevant: Core benchmark for recursive chain traversal and distributed evidence completeness.

title: EX-FEVER: A Dataset for Multi-hop Explainable Fact Verification
authors: Huanhuan Ma; Weizhi Xu; Yifan Wei; Liuji Chen; Liang Wang; Qiang Liu; Shu Wu; Liang Wang
task_description: Verify 2-hop and 3-hop claims with explanations that expose reasoning paths.
inputs: Over 60,000 claims synthesized from hyperlinked Wikipedia documents.
outputs_or_labels: Veracity labels and explanations outlining reasoning paths; retrieval, explanation generation and verification evaluation.
pipeline_gap_filled: Recursive evidence chains; inspectable reasoning paths; claim-to-source traversal.
artifact_access_status: paper page/PDF verified; dataset download not independently verified
evidence_basis: ACL abstract states >60,000 claims, 2/3-hop reasoning, veracity labels, and path explanations.
limitations: Claims are derived from Wikipedia and modified/summarized; attribution and conflicting-source modeling are absent.
why_relevant: Best direct candidate for evaluating chain-aware explanations rather than only final verdicts.

title: WiCE: Real-World Entailment for Claims in Wikipedia
authors: Ryo Kamoi; Tanya Goyal; Juan Diego Rodriguez; Greg Durrett
task_description: Evaluate fine-grained entailment between natural claims and evidence, including claim subparts and minimal evidence.
inputs: Natural Wikipedia claims and evidence pairs.
outputs_or_labels: Claim-level entailment, sub-sentence entailment judgments, and minimal supporting evidence sentence subsets.
pipeline_gap_filled: Claim decomposition; minimal evidence; claim-to-source traversal.
artifact_access_status: paper page/PDF verified; data link not independently verified
evidence_basis: ACL abstract explicitly reports sub-sentence judgments and minimal evidence subsets.
limitations: Not source-attribution aware; no explicit speaker ownership or recursive hop labels.
why_relevant: Strong diagnostic for whether every subclaim has sufficient evidence, useful as a bedrock-claim layer.

title: The Automated Verification of Textual Claims (AVeriTeC) Shared Task
authors: Michael Schlichtkrull; Yulong Chen; Chenxi Whitehouse; Zhenyun Deng; Mubashara Akhtar; Rami Aly; Zhijiang Guo; Christos Christodoulopoulos; Oana Cocarascu; Arpit Mittal; James Thorne; Andreas Vlachos
task_description: Retrieve evidence for real-world fact-checker claims and predict veracity with a joint evidence-quality criterion.
inputs: Real-world claims checked by fact-checkers; web or organizer knowledge store.
outputs_or_labels: Verdict labels, retrieved evidence, and AVeriTeC score requiring correct verdict plus adequate evidence.
pipeline_gap_filled: Real-world claim grounding; evidence sufficiency; source traversal under open-world retrieval.
artifact_access_status: paper and official dataset page verified
evidence_basis: ACL abstract states real-world fact-checker claims, web/knowledge-store evidence, and score coupling verdict with evidence quality; official dataset URL linked in scholarly artifact.
limitations: Not recursive by annotation; attribution provenance is source/document level rather than speaker/claim ownership.
why_relevant: Best realism control for open-web evidence grounding and joint answer/evidence evaluation.

title: Coordinating Search-Informed Reasoning and Reasoning-Guided Search in Claim Verification
authors: Qisheng Hu; Quanyu Long; Wenya Wang
benchmark_or_resource_name: HARIS evaluation on EX-FEVER and HoVer
task_description: Evaluate coordinated search/reasoning for multi-hop claim verification on EX-FEVER and HoVer.
outputs_or_labels: Verification performance and interpretability-oriented search/reasoning results.
pipeline_gap_filled: Recursive retrieval policy; chain search; evidence-path construction.
artifact_access_status: paper page/PDF verified; no new artifact verified
evidence_basis: ACL page states experiments on EX-FEVER and HoVer demonstrate multi-hop claim verification with coordinated search and reasoning.
limitations: Method paper, not a new benchmark; evidence of task design is indirect through reused benchmarks.
why_relevant: Useful official artifact showing current evaluation practice for recursive search-informed reasoning.

title: Enhancing Structured Evidence Extraction for Fact Verification
authors: Zirui Wu; Nan Hu; Yansong Feng
task_description: Extract and integrate sentence, table, and cell evidence for claim verification, including multi-hop and numerical reasoning.
inputs: Claims with Wikipedia text, tables, rows, and cells.
outputs_or_labels: Evidence recall/precision and FEVEROUS score combining complete gold evidence set with correct label.
pipeline_gap_filled: Heterogeneous evidence chains; structured source traversal; complete evidence-set verification.
artifact_access_status: paper and code URL verified from ACL page
evidence_basis: ACL abstract says FEVEROUS requires unstructured and structured evidence, and provides a released code URL; paper describes graph-based cell selection for multi-hop reasoning.
limitations: Not attribution-aware and mostly Wikipedia; source identity/ownership is absent.
why_relevant: Strong control for evidence graphs where a chain crosses text and structured records.

title: A Benchmark Dataset for Automatic Detection of Claims and Evidence in the Context of Controversial Topics
authors: Ehud Aharoni; Anatoly Polnarov; Tamar Lavee; Daniel Hershcovich; Ran Levy; Ruty Rinott; Dan Gutfreund; Noam Slonim
benchmark_or_resource_name: Claims and Evidence in Controversial Topics
task_description: Detect claims and evidence in controversial-topic texts.
pipeline_gap_filled: Claim/evidence span extraction; disagreement-sensitive evidence context.
artifact_access_status: paper page/PDF verified; dataset not independently verified
evidence_basis: ACL record identifies this as a benchmark dataset for automatic detection of claims and evidence.
limitations: Older span-detection task; no recursive chains or explicit attribution roles.
why_relevant: Useful low-level control for claim/evidence segmentation before recursive grounding.

title: UnifEE: Unified Evidence Extraction for Fact Verification
authors: Nan Hu; Zirui Wu; Yuxuan Lai; Chen Zhang; Yansong Feng
task_description: Extract unified evidence graphs over text sentences and table cells for fact verification.
inputs: Claims plus mixed text/table evidence candidates.
outputs_or_labels: Evidence selection and veracity prediction; graph interactions among candidates.
pipeline_gap_filled: Evidence graph traversal; multi-hop mixed-source chains.
artifact_access_status: paper page/PDF verified; artifact not independently verified
evidence_basis: ACL abstract states FEVEROUS requires sentence and table-cell evidence and that the unified graph helps especially on multi-hop claims.
limitations: No speaker/source attribution and no disagreement semantics.
why_relevant: Supports graph-level evidence-chain testing and mixed evidence modalities.

title: Can AI Validate Science? Benchmarking LLMs on Claim →Evidence Reasoning in AI Papers
authors: Shashidhar Reddy Javaji; Yupeng Cao; Haohang Li; Yangyang Yu; Nikhil Muralidhar; Zining Zhu
task_description: Evaluate scientific claim-evidence extraction and validation in AI papers.
inputs: AI research papers with claims and supporting evidence.
outputs_or_labels: Claim/evidence extraction and validation outputs with comparative LLM evaluation.
pipeline_gap_filled: Scientific claim-to-evidence links; scholarly provenance; bedrock claim support.
artifact_access_status: paper page/PDF verified; artifact not independently verified
evidence_basis: ACL abstract calls CLAIM-BENCH a comprehensive benchmark for scientific claim-evidence extraction and validation, focused on logical links within papers.
limitations: Recursive source chains and attribution roles are not central; benchmark details/artifact access need follow-up verification.
why_relevant: Most relevant scholarly-text benchmark for claim→evidence links in the project’s target domain.
